PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep the open session selected and in view when pinning it
PullRequest.Body:

* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

In the Agents window sessions list, pinning or unpinning the session open in the main window moves its row to another section and loses track of it. The row ends up outside the viewport. If the receiving section is collapsed, the row is hidden and the selection is dropped. On unpin, the session can also disappear behind a section's "+N more" cap.

## Changes

- After the Pin/Unpin actions (row hover button and context menu), if the session is the one open in the main window, the list keeps the open chat's row selected and focused. It scrolls the row into view only if it isn't already visible, and expands a collapsed section that holds it. That expansion is saved like a manual expand. If the session's chats are collapsed, the session row stands in for its open chat.
- The open session now stays visible past the "+N more" caps of sections and folders, the same way the onboarding target already did. `limitSessionsForList` takes `revealSessionIds` instead of a single `revealSessionId`. `SESSIONS_LIST.md` is updated to match.
- The fix works in both trees of the new Inbox layout.

The list's selection still means "the chat open in the main window", as in #345747. Pinning or unpinning a session that isn't open neither scrolls the list nor changes its selection. Drag-and-drop into or out of Pinned and the implicit unpin from Add to Group are unchanged.

## Review notes

- Pinning the open session into a Pinned section the user collapsed now expands that section and saves the expansion. This overrides #345233's "keep a user-collapsed Pinned" for this one case.
- Keeping the open session past the caps applies on every list update, not only right after an unpin.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open a session that is far down the list and scroll so the Pinned section is off-screen.
2. Pin the open session from its hover button or context menu. It stays selected and scrolls into view, and Pinned expands if it was collapsed.
3. Unpin it. It stays selected and visible in its section, including when it would otherwise be behind "+N more".
4. Pin a session that isn't open. The list doesn't scroll and the selection stays on the open chat.

## Validation

New tests in `sessionsList.test.ts` cover pinning while scrolled down, a user-collapsed Pinned section, a nested open chat row, pinning a session that isn't open, unpinning past a cap, and unpinning into a collapsed "Older" section. The first five failed before the fix.

- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/*.test.js"`: 8,207 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/**/*.test.js"`: 2,330 passing, 2 failing in `PromptTemplatePlaceholderController`, which also fail on `main` without this change
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: passed

Not yet checked in a running Code - OSS.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pinning or unpinning the session currently open in the main window from the row action or context menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action calls SessionsList.pinSession/unpinSession; the model persists the pin set and synchronously fires onDidChange, which performs the existing full list update. The new revealOpenChatRow then resolves the rebuilt row, reveals it only as needed, accounts for the sticky footer, and updates focus/selection before the action returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the pinned-session ID set through profile storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile-storage write per effective single-session pin or unpin; unchanged for this scenario
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pin and unpin already persisted exactly once before firing the synchronous list update
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the list-model change event and therefore before the row reveal

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist expanded section collapse state when revealing an active row expands a user-collapsed ancestor
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one write for the collapsed destination section in the tested pin/unpin move; only when an ancestor must expand
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The row was not revealed after pin/unpin, so this automatic expansion and its corresponding collapse-state write did not occur
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs during the synchronous reveal/ancestor expansion path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The existing list rebuild scales with all loaded sessions and chats. The new reveal lookup scans the session array once and a selected session's child rows; only the one session matching the main-window session proceeds to geometry/reveal work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the UI thread: storage mutation, synchronous event-driven list rebuild, then reveal/focus/selection. No subprocess, IPC, database, or network work is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pin state is held in an in-memory Set and persisted; section collapse state is read from profile storage and immediately persisted when changed. No cold/warm network cache participates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous ordering and bounded cardinality from the model event handler, action loop, reveal helper, and collapse-state listener.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Profile-storage backend latency and the maximum real session/chat count are not measured, but the new boundary cardinality is bounded to one user-triggered collapse-state write and the geometry work is bounded to one active row.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added UI-thread work is user-triggered and bounded to one active row; the only new storage write occurs when intentionally persisting a newly expanded collapsed section.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pinning or unpinning one or more sessions that are not open in the main window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each action target still mutates the model and synchronously rebuilds the visible list as before. The new revealOpenChatRow exits immediately after checking the current shown session ID, so it performs no tree traversal, geometry work, scrolling, or extra persistence for non-active targets.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the pinned-session ID set through profile storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write and one synchronous list update per effective target in the existing action loop; batch drag/drop uses the existing unpinSessions path
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-target action loop and model persistence/event behavior existed before the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on the action critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected action target count controls the pre-existing number of model writes and list rebuilds. The new helper adds only constant-time shown-session checks for non-active targets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial per target on the UI thread; there is no burst of parallel subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: In-memory pin membership avoids work for no-op mutations; no negative cache or request coalescing is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because the guard precedes all new session-array and tree work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-selection prevalence is unknown, but the diff does not increase expensive boundary cardinality or rebuild count for these targets.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the changed path exits before expensive reveal work and does not amplify existing per-target storage or update behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Routine sessions-list updates while an active or onboarding session must remain visible past section and folder caps
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A visible-list update derives up to two reveal IDs, performs normal filtering/grouping, checks capped folder sections for either ID, and for each capped section filters only the tail beyond the five-item default cap before rebuilding the virtual trees. Active-chat changes schedule this update at the next animation frame; model/filter changes may update synchronously under existing behavior.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added folder checks and capped-tail filters sum to O(number of sessions in relevant sections), using at most two reveal IDs after deduplication by Set membership. At most the active and onboarding sessions are appended beyond caps, so rendered-row growth is bounded to two sessions plus their existing chat children.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread update, with active-session updates coalesced to the next animation frame and other scheduled session/chat updates also coalesced by pendingListUpdate. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is introduced on this update path; the experiment treatment is fetched separately and retained in an observable.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session-group limit is cached in sessionGroupLimit after the asynchronous treatment fetch. Reveal IDs are recomputed from in-memory observables each update; there is no miss retry or retained unbounded cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the O(N) scan/allocation mechanism and its execution on list updates; low evidence that its bounded incremental cost creates user-visible latency over the pre-existing full rebuild.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real maximum session counts and update rates are unknown, but the surrounding update already performs multiple full-session filters, grouping, sorting, and tree reconstruction, and the added pass is linear with constant-size membership state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff adds linear scans and short-lived arrays/Sets, but not a higher asymptotic cost than the existing update, unbounded retention, extra boundary fan-out, or enough concrete hot-path impact to establish a performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Changing the chat shown in the main window while the sessions list is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing autorun schedules one animation-frame list update and selection synchronization. The changed cap logic can keep that active session's row in a capped section or folder during the rebuild, after which existing syncActiveChatSelection selects/reveals it.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The update scales with loaded sessions as above; only one main-window active session is retained beyond caps.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One coalesced animation-frame task replaces any pending active-session task; all tree work is synchronous within that frame. No external boundaries are reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shown chat is an in-memory observable, and session/chat models are reused; no cold/warm external cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the MutableDisposable animation-frame scheduling and single active-session model.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of active-chat switches and list sizes varies, but task replacement prevents an accumulating queue.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new cap inclusion participates in an already coalesced rebuild and cannot accumulate concurrent work or retained entries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced pin/unpin ordering, synchronous list rebuild and reveal/layout work, collapse-state persistence, cap scanning/allocation, active-chat scheduling, multi-target actions, and the absence of new subprocess/IPC/database/network fan-out. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.
